issues.issue: Whether the RAD should admit the US visa and proposed-marriage letter as new evidence
issues.applicant_position: Sought admission of the US visa and proposed-marriage letter as new evidence under s. 110(4).
issues.result_quote: The RAD admits the two foregoing documents.

issues.issue: Whether an oral hearing should be held before the RAD
issues.applicant_position: Asked the RAD to hold an oral hearing and find her a Convention refugee.
issues.result_quote: finds that it does not meet the criteria pursuant to ss. 110(6) of IRPA

issues.issue: Whether the RPD erred in giving little weight to her identity, employment and medical documents
issues.applicant_position: RPD wrongly discounted her documents because of visa concerns; the medical document deserved weight.
issues.respondent_position: Not stated on appeal; at the RPD the Minister said the visa application undermined her claim.
issues.result_quote: the RAD finds that the RPD erred in giving little weight, for example, to a medical document

issues.issue: Whether the RPD addressed the central allegations, including the 2014 attack and her sexual orientation
issues.applicant_position: RPD never addressed the pivotal 2014 attack or her sexual orientation, so its findings are incomplete.
issues.result_quote: The RAD finds that the RPD has failed to address the central allegations of this claim.

issues.issue: Whether the RPD properly found a lack of subjective fear (no claim in US, re-availments, delay)
issues.applicant_position: Failure to claim, re-availments and delay do not show a lack of subjective fear.
issues.result_quote: they do not address the pivotal incident which occurred in XXXX 2014 and caused the Appellant to leave Russia.

issues.issue: Whether the RAD should substitute a refugee determination
issues.applicant_position: Asked the RAD to find her a Convention refugee.
issues.result_quote: The RAD cannot substitute its own decision, as to do so would require conducting an entirely new hearing
